chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from 'Ali, from Abi Basir, who said:
Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام said: The husband may wash his wife in travel, and the woman may wash her husband in travel, when there is no man with them.

So these reports, even if they are unrestricted regarding the permissibility of the man washing the woman and the woman washing the man, we restrict them by the reports that we have previously mentioned, because when one ruling is transmitted in both restricted and unrestricted form, there is no disagreement that the unrestricted should be carried upon the restricted.

Moreover, this ruling is only permissible when women are absent if the woman has died, and men are absent if the man has died. What indicates that is what we have narrated among the previous reports, and that further clarifies it.

key_terms.الْمُطْلَقُ: the unqualified form of a ruling
key_terms.الْمُقَيَّدِ: the qualified form of a ruling
key_terms.يُغَسِّلُ: to perform the ritual washing of the deceased

ai.seo_question: When may a husband or wife wash their deceased spouse according to this hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of a husband and wife washing one another after death, especially in the circumstance of travel. It explains that narrations permitting this are to be understood in light of more restricted reports, establishing that such washing is allowed in cases of necessity when same-gender persons are unavailable.
